answer: Verify without reading. Each submission posts a nullifier seal, black as onyx, bound to one identity and one epoch, proving the answer satisfies the rubric without revealing it. Nullifiers sink into the ocean of public keys and never resurface: reuse across clones is impossible, and the timber frame of each answer stays private until settlement — fleets cannot copy or batch-generate certificates. Every fake identity must run its own honest generation to mint its own proof. Cost per cloned answer equals an honest one, with zero amortization: the certificate is the anti-sybil.
